lines.trans: Due to circumstances, we had to cancel your appearance today, Mr. Muranishi.
Why is that?
With an uproar this big, there is no way we can put you on air.
You are shutting me out over a ridiculous reason like that?
Ms. Kuroki is still welcome on stage, so please come this way.
Hold on. If that is how it is, Kaoru Kuroki isn't going on either.
Give me a break, Ms. Kuroki has a regular spot on our show!

words.gram: Plain imperative of くれる (give/do for me).

lines.trans: No. Without the director's permission, I will not appear.
Hey, I know! You should come work as an actor at our studio!
We don't need television anyway. Let's go.
As long as you fear new challenges, you will never make progress.
We are holding your company responsible for this!

examples.text: 諸事情で今日の村西さんの出演、見送ることになっちゃいまして。
examples.trans: Due to circumstances, we had to cancel your appearance today, Mr. Muranishi.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Special reading きょう.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

examples.text: そんなことしたら世の中がめちゃくちゃになりますよ！
examples.trans: If you aired things like that on television, society would fall apart!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Noun form of 騒ぐ (make a fuss).

examples.trans: It turned into a big commotion.

meanings.note: Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.note: Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

そんな.gloss: such; that kind of; that much

meanings.note: Before たくさん, means 'that huge an amount'.

examples.text: そんな話は知りません。
examples.trans: I do not know such a story.

examples.text: そんな高いものは買えません。
examples.trans: I cannot buy something that expensive.

meanings.note: Noun meaning reason or grounds.

examples.text: 遅れた理由を教えてください。
examples.trans: Please tell me the reason you were late.

examples.text: お薦めする理由がもう一つあります。
examples.trans: There is one more reason I recommend it.

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Core everyday reassurance or check covering safety, health, and reliability.

examples.text: 心配しないで、大丈夫だよ。
examples.trans: Do not worry, it is fine.

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: て-form 待って + ください is 'please wait'; causative お待たせして means 'having kept you waiting'.
Colloquial conjunction built from だ + たら.

meanings.en: open a store; bring out; hand in
meanings.note: 店を出す means opening a branch; 出しやがって attaches tough-guy disdainful やがる.

examples.text: 駅前に新しい店を出します。
examples.trans: We open a new branch in front of the station.

examples.text: 書類を出してください。

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: 黒木さん、あなたテレビいいですよ。レギュラー考えますからね。
examples.trans: Ms. Kuroki, you are fantastic on television. We will consider making you a regular.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Godan verb; 持ってくる means 'bring'.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Humble (kenjougo) equivalent of する, used in polite business and apologetic expressions.

examples.text: すぐにご連絡いたします。
examples.trans: I will contact you right away.

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Attaches to the masu-stem of a verb to form a firm but polite command.

examples.text: 村西監督、テレビ出演おめでとう！
examples.trans: Director Muranishi, congratulations on your television appearance!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Colloquial quotative/emphatic particle expressing surprise or dismissal.

examples.text: そんなことなんて知らない。
examples.trans: I don't know anything like that.

examples.text: 嘘だなんて信じられない。
examples.trans: I can't believe it's a lie.

meanings.note: Casual counterpart of こちら.
Modifies nouns directly, as in 新しい店 ('new store') and 新しい仕事 ('new job').

examples.text: 新しい仕事が始まりました。
新しい靴を買いました。
